draft.title: Defining urban and rural places
card: a place with a high population density, where many people live close together. Most jobs are not in farming, such as work in shops, offices, hospitals and factories.
a place with a lower population density, where people live further apart. More of the land is used for farming or is left as bushland or other natural areas.
Population density is the number of people living in an area, such as people per square kilometre. It is one of the main ways to tell urban from rural.
The two types of place sit on a spectrum. A small town can have some features of both, so geographers look at density, jobs and land use together.
draft.remember: Urban means crowded, with mostly non-farm jobs. Rural means more space, with more farming or natural land.

a.q: Which description best fits an urban place?
opts: Many people close together, with mostly non-farm jobs
Few people spread out, with mostly farming jobs
Many people close together, with mostly farming jobs
Few people spread out, with mostly non-farm jobs
a.why: Urban places combine high population density with jobs that are mostly outside farming. The option with farming jobs and high density mixes up the two features, because farming jobs are more typical of rural places.
a.clue: Think about both density and the kind of work.

b.q: Wendy compares two places. Place X has 4 people per square km, with wheat farms and bushland. Place Y has 3000 people per square km, with offices and shops. Which statement is correct?
opts: X is more rural because of its low density and land use
Y is more rural because it has more jobs in services
X is more urban because it has more open land
Y is more rural because it has more people
b.why: X has a low density and most of its land is used for farming or nature, which are rural features. Y is urban, because its high density and shop and office jobs are urban features. Having more people in a place does not make it more rural.
b.clue: Check density, jobs and land use for each place.

a.best: Many people close together, with mostly non-farm jobs

b.best: X is more rural because of its low density and land use

proposal.title: Defining urban and rural places
card: a place with a high population density, where many people live close together. Most jobs are not in farming, such as work in shops, offices, hospitals and factories.
a place with a lower population density, where people live further apart. More of the land is used for farming or is left as bushland or other natural areas.

proposal.remember: Urban means crowded, with mostly non-farm jobs. Rural means more space, with more farming or natural land.

a.q: Merino Flat is a small town. Most residents work in its shops, school and hospital, and wheat farms surround it. How should a geographer classify it?
opts: Mixed: urban jobs, but rural land use around it
Urban, because jobs alone decide the type of place
Rural, because its total number of residents is small
Rural, because farmland alone decides the type of place
a.why: The town's jobs are mostly outside farming, an urban feature, while the farmland around it is a rural feature. Places sit on a spectrum, so geographers weigh density, jobs and land use together. Judging by the number of residents is tempting, but density, not total population, is the measure, and no single feature decides on its own.
a.clue: Does one feature settle it, or should you weigh several?

problems.detail: The why says 'density, not total population, is the measure'. That is too absolute for Australia. The ABS classes places as urban or rural partly by the population size of a centre: urban centres have 1,000 or more people. A careful teacher could defend 'small population means rural', so the why should soften this claim rather than dismiss total population outright.
Too easy for Year 12 HSC. The distractors are plainly absurd (for example, 'X is more urban because it has more open land'), so the question barely tests understanding.
